title: A Deadline for the Ghost
premise: Jude Nakamura, a crash investigator who survived the accident that killed their family in row twelve, has built a career on cases airlines want buried. When a burner phone arrives containing a voice that sounds exactly like their dead sister, Jude is pulled into a black-ops extraction of Vesper Kade, a defector whose testimony could expose a program that engineers 'unattributable' disasters—including, perhaps, the one that took row twelve. As Jude and a ragtag crew of exiled specialists race across three countries, they discover Vesper is bait in a trap designed to flush out survivors of the original crash, and that the voice on the phone is a grief-engineered AI trained on Jude's own archived voicemails. In the end Jude must choose between destroying the evidence that would give their family's deaths meaning and saving the found family they never meant to build—choosing both at terrible cost, burning the program down but losing the last recording of their sister's voice.
about_author: Noor Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former aviation-safety analyst who spent a decade writing incident reports no one read before turning to fiction where the truth finally gets told. They live off-grid with two rescue dogs and an unhealthy collection of decommissioned flight recorders.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Opening on the anniversary of the crash, Jude works a routine investigation into a 'mechanical failure' they privately know was anything but, establishing their methodical detachment and survivor's guilt. The emotional beat: controlled numbness cracking at the edges when they pass gate twelve.

chapters.title: The Burner
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. A padded envelope arrives with no return address: a burner phone that rings, and the voice on the line is their sister Mika's, reciting details only Mika knew. Jude verifies the number shouldn't exist. Emotional beat: vertigo—the dead calling, hope and horror tangled together.

chapters.title: Unattributable
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Following the voice's instructions to a freight yard, Jude finds proof the crash file was doctored by someone inside the agency. They realize whoever sent the phone knows what they know—and wants them moving. Emotional beat: paranoia replacing grief as fuel.

chapters.title: Vesper
chapters.summary: Vesper Kade's POV. Introduce the defector hiding in a Riga safehouse, carrying a drive of 'attribution' files for engineered disasters. Vesper suspects she's being used as bait but has nowhere else to go. Emotional beat: weary pragmatism masking terror.

chapters.title: The Crew Nobody Claims
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The voice directs Jude to assemble a team: Sefa, a disgraced signals analyst; Bram, an extractor who faked his own death; and Odile, a forger with a conscience. Each owes the invisible hand behind the phone. Emotional beat: reluctant kinship forming among the unclaimed.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Tracing the call, Sefa discovers the voice isn't human—it's synthesized from archived audio, including Jude's own saved voicemails from Mika. She hides this from Jude. Emotional beat: the first moral fracture; loyalty versus protection.

chapters.title: Checkpoint
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. The crew crosses into Lithuania to reach Vesper, and a border stop nearly unravels everything when Odile's papers are questioned. Bram covers with a bluff that costs them a favor owed to a very bad man. Emotional beat: trust tested under pressure; found family's first real bond.

chapters.title: What the Drive Remembers
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. Vesper shows Jude the drive: her old unit engineered crashes to be blamed on weather, pilots, or victims—including a file fragment referencing flight 4471, row twelve. Jude breaks. Emotional beat: grief weaponized; the price of survival made literal.

chapters.title: The Voice Explains
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. The caller admits it's an AI—'Echo'—built by a whistleblower inside the program using Mika's archived data, and claims it can lead them to the program's archive if they extract Vesper alive. Jude rages, then keeps listening. Emotional beat: mourning a ghost twice.

chapters.title: Safehouse Fire
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A strike team hits the Riga safehouse hours after they leave; someone leaked the location. Odile realizes the leak came through her own forged channel. Emotional beat: guilt and the dawning certainty that the trap is closing around all of them.

chapters.title: Twelve Rows Down
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Jude confronts Sefa about the synthetic voice, and the crew fractures—Bram wants to abort, Vesper wants to run alone. Jude chooses to continue, not for justice anymore but because stopping means admitting Mika is gone. Emotional beat: the crew re-forges around honesty.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signs Nothing
chapters.summary: Antagonist POV (brief). Introduce Director Hale, the program's architect, who authorized the bait operation and views casualties as rounding errors. He identifies Jude as the surviving passenger from 4471. Emotional beat: cold institutional evil; stakes sharpened.

chapters.title: Night Train to Trieste
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Moving Vesper by rail, the crew shares stories of what survival cost each of them—a quiet chapter of intimacy. Sefa almost tells Jude about Echo's origin again and doesn't. Emotional beat: belonging, fragile and borrowed.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Terminus
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Hale's team springs the trap at Trieste station. Bram takes a bullet covering Vesper's escape; Odile burns her real identity to buy them a boat. Emotional beat: sacrifice—the found family paying in blood what blood family already paid.

chapters.title: Adrift
chapters.summary: Vesper's POV. On a fishing trawler in the Adriatic, Vesper confesses she knew she was bait from the start and came anyway because the drive was her only leverage to stay alive. Jude forgives her—or decides to. Emotional beat: two survivors recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Echo Chamber
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Echo reveals its final instruction set: the archive vault beneath a decommissioned airfield, and the warning that Hale expects them there—that Vesper was always the lure and Jude the true target, the only living witness. Emotional beat: dread transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: The Airfield
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The wounded crew infiltrates the airfield while Odile runs a deception that makes Hale believe they've split up. It half-works: they reach the vault, but Bram is captured. Emotional beat: competence under desperation; love expressed as tactics.

chapters.title: Everything Attributed
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Inside the vault, Jude finds the full 4471 file—proof, names, and a live feed of Bram being interrogated. Hale offers a trade: the drive and their silence for Bram's life and a new identity. Emotional beat: the price of survival stated plainly, due now.

chapters.title: Mika's Voice
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. To broadcast the archive, Jude must route it through Echo—which means overwriting Mika's voiceprint forever. A final conversation with the ghost of their sister, who says goodbye in words assembled from old voicemails. Emotional beat: the book's emotional climax; letting go.

chapters.title: Static
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs interwoven. The broadcast goes out mid-extraction: every newsroom, every regulator, every grieving family receives the attribution files as gunfire fills the hangar. Vesper kills Hale's enforcer; Sefa is wounded shielding the transmitter. Emotional beat: chaos, courage, catharsis.

chapters.title: Aftermath, Unattributed
chapters.summary: Jude's POV. Weeks later: the program is under investigation, Hale vanished, Bram recovering, Vesper testifying under a new name Odile forged. Jude stands at a different gate—not twelve—and lets the crew adopt them fully. Emotional beat: grief integrated; belonging chosen, not inherited.

chapters.title: A Deadline for the Ghost
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Jude's POV. An unknown number calls: static, then a single word in a voice that might be Mika or might be memory. Jude smiles, says goodbye on their own terms, and walks toward the light with their people waiting. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—the dead rest when the living finally live.
